children: Vancouver, British Columbia – November 25, 2026 – TheNewswire - Tungsten Eagle Development Corp.

("Tungsten Eagle" or the "Company") announces that it has entered into an agreement dated October 30, 2026 (the "Agreement") with Integral Wealth Securities Limited ("Integral") for market-making services to assist in maintaining an orderly trading market and contributing to the liquidity of the Company's common shares, in compliance with the policies of the Canadian Securities Exchange (the "CSE") and applicable securities laws.

Market-making activities commenced on November 2, 2026. Under the Agreement, the Company will pay Integral a monthly cash fee of $6,500, plus applicable taxes, for an initial term of three months. Following the initial term, the engagement will continue on a month-to-month basis until terminated by either party on 30 days' written notice. The Agreement does not include performance-based factors, and Integral will not receive common shares, options or other securities of the Company as compensation.

The Company and Integral are dealing at arm's length. They are unrelated and unaffiliated entities, and neither Integral nor its principals have an interest, directly or indirectly, in the Company or in the securities of the Company, although Integral may acquire an interest in securities of the Company in the course of its market-making activities. All trades undertaken by Integral will be made as principal using its own capital and securities, and the Company has not provided any funds to Integral to facilitate the market-making activity.

Integral Wealth Securities Limited is an independent investment dealer and a member of the Canadian Investment Regulatory Organization (CIRO), engaged in market making, investment banking and wealth management. Integral is headquartered in Toronto and operates from offices across Canada.

Tungsten Eagle Development Corp. is a mineral exploration company focused on American critical metals. The Company is advancing the Liberty Ridge Tungsten Project in Elko County, Nevada. Tungsten is designated a critical mineral by the U.S. Geological Survey, and the U.S. currently has no domestic tungsten mine production.
